clue.text: Regular visitors may be a little taken in by colours

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held within it, so these letters sit inside the colour word

parts.note: hues are colours or shades
a bit is a little amount

explanation.surface: Frequent guests might be slightly impressed or fooled by the paintwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' pretends to mean fooled; here it means held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: people who frequent a place regularly are its regulars, the French-derived word for such patrons.

clue.text: Most self-effacing and happy supporting topless pal

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting below, so the happy word comes beneath
topless means losing the top letter, which in a down answer is the first

parts.note: a chum is a pal
blest, or blessed, means happy or fortunate

explanation.surface: A modest, contented person propping up a friend who has bared their chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes C from CHUM to leave HUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the superlative of modest or unassuming, the least proud of all.

clue.text: Objects of ridicule only on test, oddly

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd positions of the word test, first and third

explanation.surface: A joke at someone's expense only on a strange exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks T and S from TeSt.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: people who are the targets of jokes, as in the butt of every gag.

clue.text: Tunics may be key when crossing road

parts.note: TAB is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the word for when straddles the road

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: Instructions on which clothing key matters when crossing a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: sleeveless overgarments, like those worn by heralds or medieval knights.

clue.text: View across lake — rising fish

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards
across means spanning, so the word for view stretches either side of the lake letter

parts.note: to see is to view

explanation.surface: Looking out over a lake as fish come up to the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts L inside SEE as SLEE; 'rising' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: snake-like fish such as the conger or the jellied kind of London tradition.

clue.text: Admonish a pessimist accommodating models

indicators.note: accommodating means housing or holding, so the run of words holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: Telling off a gloomy person while also putting up some fashion models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' signals letters held within admoniSH A PESsimist.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the verb sense: to model clay is to form or mould it into a given form.

clue.text: Entertainer who'd broadcast at home on one

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the air, so what is heard rather than what is written

parts.note: this contraction, said aloud, gives the opening syllable of the name
in means at home, as in staying in
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A performer who would be on air at home on one channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals the sound of the contraction who'd, which opens the escapologist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Hungarian-American escapologist and illusionist, the most famous of stage performers.

clue.text: Tramping around nursing a grouse

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the shuffled letters cradle the single letter
around means turned about, so the letters of tramping are shuffled

explanation.surface: Hiking about while tending a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges TRAMPING into PTRMIGAN, and 'nursing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a mountain bird of the grouse family that turns white in winter.

clue.text: Tight-fitting fleece with natty fringes

parts.note: to fleece is to skin, cheat someone out of money

indicators.note: fringes are outer edges, so take the first and last letters of natty

explanation.surface: A smart, close-fitting fleece jacket with tidy trims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringes' takes N and Y from NattY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in fashion: snugly fitted to the body, as in narrow-leg jeans.

clue.text: Indefinitely postpones the two shopping centres having switched leaders

indicators.note: the two words exchange their opening letters, so leaders are swapped between them

parts.note: both means the two together
malls are shopping centres

explanation.surface: A tale of a council putting off plans for two new shopping malls.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the B of BOTH and the M of MALLS gives MOTH BALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to put a plan in storage like an unused coat is to shelve it with no date to revive it.

clue.text: Old Greeks showing expertise in bridges

indicators.note: in means placed inside, here inside the bridges word

parts.note: spans are bridges, structures that span a gap
art is skill or expertise

explanation.surface: Ancient Greeks displaying engineering skill in building bridges.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: citizens of the austere, warlike ancient city-state in the Peloponnese.

clue.text: Taste of Burma regularly confronting French pal?

indicators.note: confronting means facing, so the first piece stands right in front of the second
regularly means taking every other letter of the word Burma, here the second and fourth

parts.note: ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A query about a flavour from Burma meeting a French friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks U and M from bUrMa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese-named fifth basic flavour, a savoury, meaty sensation alongside sweet, sour, salt and bitter.

clue.text: Prestige attraction around borders of Somerset

indicators.note: around means one word wraps about the other, the lure enclosing the picked letters

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or enticement

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A prestigious tourist draw somewhere on the edges of the English county of Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: glory, distinction or renown, as when a famous name adds sheen to an event.

clue.text: Charm of eccentric A-list chap?

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of the word A-list are rearranged

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Is the appeal of some odd celebrity fellow just his charisma?
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges ALIST into TALIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an amulet or lucky object believed to protect its bearer or bring good fortune.

clue.text: Praise cook drinking coffee

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the cooking word swallows the coffee

parts.note: to fry is to cook
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: Compliment the chef sipping a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym, though with a sense of excessive or insincere compliments meant to please.

clue.text: Funny team breaking up

parts.note: a side is a team, as in cricket or football
splitting means breaking up or separating

explanation.surface: A comic band or group of players finally disbanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' also means laughing helplessly, which echoes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: so hilarious that one's flanks ache from laughter.

clue.text: Dryer found in freak accidents

indicators.note: freak, as an adjective, means bizarre or abnormal, so the letters of accidents are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clothes or hair dryer turns up in some odd mishaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dryer' suggests a household appliance; it is a drying agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A drying agent, like silica gel sachets packed to absorb moisture.

clue.text: Change in fortune may be true about most of poetry

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for true wraps the shortened poetry

parts.note: real means true or genuine

indicators.note: most of means drop the last letter

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A shift of luck could be accurate about much of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a setback or turnaround, a reversal of luck.

clue.text: Popular country house on film must be target area

indicators.note: in a down or across clue, on means coming next to, here the first two pieces sit before the country house

parts.note: to shoot is to film a scene
in means popular or fashionable
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: A trendy stately home used as a film location must be the place for shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end after 'must be'; 'on film' looks like a location shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where people practise firing at targets, so a zone set aside for aiming.

clue.text: Make a speech about exercise and work

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speech word wraps the exercise

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
PE is physical education, or exercise

explanation.surface: Give a talk about fitness and employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: function or run, as a machine does when it goes.

clue.text: Regret importing European metal train

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the regret word holds the other pieces

parts.note: to rue is to regret
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Lamenting that Europe brings metal in for a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importing' puts ETIN inside RUE; 'train' is the procession sense, not a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the train of attendants or followers accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Dresses down, as result of viral infection on board

indicators.note: on, in the crossword phrase on board, means placed inside the ship, so the infection sits between the ship's letters

parts.note: in the convention on board, board stands for the ship, SS being a steamship
a cold is a viral infection

explanation.surface: A tale of a ship's crew sick with a viral bug, as a result of which someone gets a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention for putting something inside SS (steamship): COLD goes between its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to dress someone down is to tell them off or rebuke them.

clue.text: Crazy editor going after nameless Londoner

indicators.note: going after means following, so the editor comes last
nameless means without N, the standard abbreviation for name

parts.note: a Cockney is a working-class Londoner born within earshot of Bow bells

explanation.surface: An anonymous East End resident is chased by a mad journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N (name) from COCKNEY to give COCKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in its informal sense: absurd, askew or ridiculous, as a hare-brained scheme might be.

clue.text: Tried hard, putting roast initially in cooker

indicators.note: in means placed inside, here inside the cooker

parts.note: a stove is a cooker

indicators.note: initially means take just the opening letter of the word roast

explanation.surface: A cook makes a real effort, getting the joint into the oven to roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R from roast; 'in' places it within STOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the past tense of strive, meaning made a great effort.

clue.text: Title holder's now upset Her Majesty

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disturbed, so the letters of now are rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A champion has now disturbed the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges NOW to OWN; 'Title' suggests a sporting title rather than legal title to property.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal sense: whoever holds title, or legal ownership, of a property.

clue.text: Block put on new farm building

indicators.note: in a down answer, put on means placed above, so the block letters come first

parts.note: to bar is to block

explanation.surface: A block placed on a new agricultural building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' sets BAR above N.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a large agricultural shed for storing hay or housing livestock.

clue.text: Durrell? A major keeper of this animal

indicators.note: a keeper holds something, so these words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Was Gerald Durrell, the famous naturalist and zoo founder, a major keeper of some beast?
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeper of' signals letters held in durreLL A MAjor; Durrell's zoo fame makes 'keeper' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American camelid, a woolly pack beast of the Andes, exactly the creature a zoo might house.

clue.text: Remuneration will come after the last of my wishes

indicators.note: will come after means the pay word follows the single letter
the last of a word is its final letter, here from my

parts.note: earnings are remuneration, money paid for work

explanation.surface: Pay will follow after my desires are met.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last of' takes Y from my; 'will come after' sets EARNINGS behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: longings or desires, strong wishes for something.

clue.text: A poser's catch?

definitions.meaning: a poser is someone who poses, such as a model for a portrait painter; the 's stands for is
in cricket, an easy catch that should never be dropped

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a person posing for an artist, and the easiest of catches in cricket.

clue.text: Change relating to the whole

definitions.note: the definition is an adjectival phrase, as in belonging to the whole

indicators.note: change as an instruction means alter the order of the letters of relating

explanation.surface: An alteration concerning everything at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges RELATING; the definition borrows the sense 'relating to the whole', with 'relating' doing double work in the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means essential to or forming part of a complete thing, hence of the entirety.
